driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks ended mixed after strong jobs data and a modest rebound for AI companies failed to quell investor nerves about the sustainability of the AI boom (5:01 PM ET). Bloomberg reported that the Treasury market pared a steep weekly advance after strong October employment data revived wagers on a Federal Reserve rate hike next month (8:47 AM ET), and that selling by trend-following systematic funds amplified Thursday's record plunge in Nasdaq 100 market value (1:49 PM ET). WSJ reported Taiwan activated market-stabilization measures after the global AI-related selloff (6:16 AM ET), and that oil futures ended little changed but sharply lower on the week on hopes for a negotiated solution to the Middle East conflict (4:14 PM ET).

items.headline: Alibaba sets Nov 18 board meeting for September-quarter results; announcement Nov 19
items.summary: In a Form 6-K filed with the SEC (accepted 6:01 AM ET), Alibaba said its board will meet to discuss unaudited results for the three months and six months ended September 30, 2026, with the results announcement on November 18, 2026 and the results approved and announced on November 19, 2026, per the filing's wording. The stock closed up 1.28% on Nov 6.

items.headline: Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Texas Gigafactory
items.summary: Per SCMP, Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday in an X post, after years of persistently weak sales; WSJ's headline likewise says the truck will wind down production amid slow sales, and MarketWatch's says the run comes to an end. Tesla closed up 4.23% on Nov 6. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

driver.text: Per Bloomberg, US stock futures started Monday on firmer footing after the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025, with dip-buyers stepping in despite a sharp drop in Nvidia (5:20 PM ET Sun). The Financial Times reported global stocks steadied after last week's AI rout, which pushed many indices into bear-market territory (5:14 AM ET), and WSJ reported Asian equities mostly rebounded while sentiment stays fragile after South Korean and Taiwanese authorities intervened (3:17 AM ET). Bloomberg reported hedge funds sold global tech stocks at one of the fastest paces on record last week (3:58 AM ET) and that Citi strategists cut US stocks and the global tech sector while upgrading Europe (4:55 AM ET). WSJ reported US and eurozone bond yields turned higher (4:52 AM ET), and oil stayed below $100 a barrel on hopes for easing Middle East tensions (2:27 AM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.
